name: AI Image Disclosure – AIDisclara
author: Ivijan-Stefan Stipic

sections.description:
EU AI Label for WordPress – AIDisclara is a free, fully customizable AI image disclosure plugin that helps website owners clearly label AI-generated and AI-modified images, improve transparency, and support EU AI Act disclosure requirements.

The plugin gives editors a clear, manual workflow for declaring whether a Media Library image was AI-generated, AI-modified, or requires a custom disclosure.

The declaration is stored on the WordPress attachment and can follow the image wherever AIDisclara supports its use. Fully customizable disclosure badges can be displayed on Featured Images and, when enabled, on marked images inside singular content.

With EU AI Label functionality, AIDisclara helps publishers, content creators, and website administrators communicate AI involvement through visible disclosure badges and structured image metadata, all completely free of charge.

AIDisclara does not attempt to detect AI-generated images. An authorized editor or administrator makes the declaration, and the plugin records and presents that editorial decision.

Documentation and Guides

Explore the official AIDisclara documentation for detailed setup instructions, editorial workflows, customization, and developer integrations.

  • Complete Documentation
  • Installation and First-Time Setup
  • Media Library Declarations and Custom Labels
  • Badge Disclaimers, Tooltips and Accessibility
  • Developer API, Hooks and Filters

Additional guides covering badge styling, multilingual configuration, structured data, media auditing, privacy, and troubleshooting are available in the complete documentation.

Key features

  • Free, fully customizable EU AI Label and disclosure badges for WordPress
  • Manual AI-generated, AI-modified, and custom declarations for images
  • Media Library integration with declaration fields, filters, and bulk actions
  • Automatic disclosure badges for supported Featured Images
  • Optional disclosure badges for marked images in posts, Pages, and public custom post types
  • Customizable badge text, position, size, colors, borders, icons, spacing, and padding
  • Multilingual badge text and tooltip disclaimers with WPML, Polylang, and TranslatePress support
  • Built-in AIDisclara logo, custom logo, or official European Commission Basic icon
  • Live badge preview and configurable display settings
  • Optional public disclosure details, including AI tool, model, dates, source, reviewer, and notes
  • Disclosure audit dashboard with filtering, statistics, bulk actions, and CSV export
  • Schema.org ImageObject JSON-LD and IPTC Digital Source Type metadata for supported images
sections.installation:
Install from a ZIP file

  1. In your WordPress admin area, go to Plugins > Add New Plugin.
  2. Select Upload Plugin and choose the AIDisclara ZIP file.
  3. Install and activate AIDisclara.
  4. Open an image in Media Library and check AI-generated image.
  5. Configure Featured Image and optional post-content badges in Settings > AIDisclara.

Install manually

  1. Upload the aiviso-ai-image-disclosure folder to /wp-content/plugins/ using FTP or your hosting file manager.
  2. Activate AIDisclara from the Plugins screen.
  3. Configure the badge in Settings > AIDisclara.
sections.faq:
What is AIDisclara and how does EU AI Label work?

AIDisclara is a free, fully customizable AI image disclosure plugin for WordPress. It helps publishers clearly identify AI-generated and AI-modified content through visible disclosure badges, editorial declarations, and supported machine-readable metadata.

The EU AI Label workflow is based on manual declarations. Authorized editors and administrators decide which media require disclosure, and AIDisclara stores those decisions as WordPress attachment metadata.

Does AIDisclara automatically detect or verify AI-generated content?

No. AIDisclara does not use AI detection, inspect image contents to determine authenticity, or verify whether an image was generated or modified by AI.

An authorized editor or administrator makes the declaration, and the plugin records and presents that editorial decision. It does not provide cryptographically verified provenance or authenticity guarantees.

Why use AIDisclara if it does not detect AI-generated images?

AIDisclara provides a predictable, transparent editorial disclosure workflow without relying on potentially inaccurate AI detection.

Authorized users can declare media as AI-generated, AI-modified, or requiring a custom disclosure. The declaration is stored on the WordPress attachment and can be reused wherever AIDisclara supports its display.

This approach gives publishers direct control over their disclosures, badge appearance, and associated metadata.

Do I need to declare the same image on every post?

No. AIDisclara stores declarations on WordPress Media Library attachments rather than individual posts.

Once an attachment is declared, its disclosure status can follow it across supported Featured Image and post-content uses, subject to the configured display settings.

Can AIDisclara display disclosure badges on images inside posts and Pages?

Yes. When content-image disclosure is enabled, AIDisclara can display badges on declared Media Library images inside individual posts, Pages, and supported public custom post types.

The content must be included in the configured post type scope and rendered through the standard WordPress content filter. Only eligible images that meet the plugin’s processing conditions receive badges.

Can Featured Image badges appear on archive and listing pages?

Yes. Set the Featured Image Badge display option to Everywhere in AIDisclara settings.

This allows eligible Featured Images to display disclosure badges outside singular views, including supported archive and listing pages.

This setting does not enable content-image processing on archive or listing views.

Does AIDisclara support AI video disclosure?

Not yet. AIDisclara currently focuses on AI image disclosure. Support for AI-generated and AI-modified video disclosure is planned as the next major feature and will be introduced in a future update.

Does AIDisclara work with custom post types?

Yes. AIDisclara supports public custom post types that use standard WordPress Featured Image APIs.

Content-image disclosure can also work with supported public custom post types when enabled and included in the configured post type scope.

Administrators can control which eligible post types participate in disclosure processing.

Does AIDisclara work with Gutenberg and the Block Editor?

Yes. AIDisclara provides Featured Image AI-status feedback in the WordPress Block Editor.

It also supports standard Gutenberg Image block output in individual post content when content-image disclosure is enabled.

Supported WordPress Video blocks can participate in optional video disclosure when the feature is enabled.

Does AIDisclara work with the Classic Editor?

Yes. The Classic Editor retains the Featured Image disclosure status interface.

Standard Media Library images inserted into individual post content can receive badges when content-image disclosure is enabled and the configured conditions are satisfied.

Will AIDisclara work with every WordPress theme?

AIDisclara is designed to work with themes that follow standard WordPress rendering APIs.

Automatic Featured Image disclosure relies on standard Featured Image functions. Content-image disclosure depends on the theme rendering the queried post’s main content through the standard WordPress content filter.

Highly customized themes, page builders, or rendering systems may bypass these integration points. Additional developer integration may be required in such cases.

Can I customize the AI disclosure badges?

Yes. AIDisclara provides fully customizable disclosure badges, including text, position, size, colors, borders, icon spacing, padding, and supported logo options.

Administrators can configure badge appearance globally and review changes through the live preview in Settings.

Disclosure declarations and display settings can be updated or reversed without modifying the original media files.

Can I use my own AI disclosure logo?

Yes. AIDisclara supports its built-in logo, a custom raster image selected from the WordPress Media Library, or the official European Commission Basic icon.

Custom SVG logo uploads are not accepted through the logo selection feature.

Can I change the disclosure text for individual images?

Yes. Global Badge text settings control the default text for AI-generated and AI-modified media.

For attachment-specific wording, select Custom disclosure on an individual Media Library attachment and enter the desired text.

This allows publishers to provide more precise disclosures when the default labels are insufficient.

Can disclosure badges and disclaimers be translated?

Yes. AIDisclara supports manual multilingual badge text with WPML, Polylang, and TranslatePress.

When a supported multilingual plugin is active with multiple configured languages, AIDisclara provides separate Badge text fields for those languages.

The same language-aware functionality is available for attachment-specific Custom disclosure text.

Optional tooltip disclaimers for AI-generated and AI-modified badges can also be configured with multilingual support.

What happens if I leave Badge text empty?

The disclosure badge displays the selected logo without visible text.

This behavior also applies independently to language-specific Badge text fields when multilingual configuration is enabled.

Does AIDisclara support machine-readable AI disclosure?

Yes. AIDisclara supports Schema.org ImageObject JSON-LD and IPTC Digital Source Type metadata for declared images.

AI-generated images can use the IPTC trainedAlgorithmicMedia value, while AI-modified images can use compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia. Custom declarations can use a supported IPTC Digital Source Type selected by the editor.

When enabled, AIDisclara generates deduplicated ImageObject JSON-LD for eligible disclosed images in supported rendering contexts.

This metadata represents a publisher-supplied editorial declaration. It does not provide cryptographically verified provenance, establish image authenticity, or create C2PA credentials.

Can I include additional AI disclosure information?

Yes. AIDisclara supports optional public disclosure details for declared media.

Depending on the configured fields, publishers can provide information such as the AI tool, model, relevant dates, source, reviewer, and public notes.

These details can help visitors better understand the declared involvement of AI in published media.

Does AIDisclara provide an audit and bulk management interface?

Yes. AIDisclara includes Media Library declaration filters, bulk actions, and a dedicated disclosure audit interface.

Authorized users can review declaration statuses, apply supported bulk operations, inspect disclosure counts, and export audit information as CSV.

These features are designed to simplify editorial management on websites with larger media libraries.

Is AIDisclara private, local, and free of external AI services?

Yes. AIDisclara is free and operates locally within WordPress without requiring an external AI detection service or an AIDisclara cloud account.

Declarations and settings are stored in WordPress. The plugin does not automatically upload images to external AI providers, perform AI analysis, collect telemetry or analytics, or load remote fonts.

When an administrator opens Settings > AIDisclara, the recommendations card may retrieve public plugin-directory metadata from WordPress.org. Normalized results are cached for 12 hours, and plugin icons may load from trusted WordPress.org domains.

These requests do not include site images, post content, visitor data, or analytics.

The Settings screen also contains an optional, user-initiated Ko-fi support link. AIDisclara does not automatically load Ko-fi JavaScript, tracking, images, or other resources. Ko-fi is contacted only when a user chooses to follow the external link.

Does AIDisclara modify original image or video files?

No. AIDisclara stores disclosure declarations as WordPress attachment metadata and renders visible badges as separate HTML and CSS overlays.

It does not alter original media files or generated WordPress image sizes.

Declarations, badge styling, visible text, and disclosure details can be changed or removed without modifying the underlying media.

Does AIDisclara guarantee EU AI Act compliance?

No. AIDisclara is a technical EU AI Label and disclosure tool designed to support AI transparency workflows. It does not provide legal advice, make legal determinations, or guarantee compliance with the EU AI Act or any other regulation.

The plugin does not determine whether Article 50 of the EU AI Act or another legal obligation applies to particular content, publishers, or organizations.

Laws, regulatory guidance, and platform requirements may change. Website owners and publishers remain responsible for determining applicable disclosure, labeling, provenance, accessibility, consumer-protection, and other requirements.

AIDisclara provides tools for recording and presenting editorial declarations, not automated legal compliance.

What happens when I deactivate AIDisclara?

When AIDisclara is deactivated, frontend disclosure badges are no longer rendered by the plugin.

Existing settings and attachment declarations remain stored in WordPress and are available if the plugin is activated again.

What happens when I delete AIDisclara?

When AIDisclara is uninstalled, its settings option is removed.

Attachment declarations remain stored by default. If you want AIDisclara’s attachment declarations removed during uninstall, enable Remove data when plugin is deleted before deleting the plugin.

Does AIDisclara provide developer hooks and filters for custom integrations?

Yes. AIDisclara provides public helper functions, filters, and actions for developers who need to integrate disclosure functionality with custom WordPress themes, plugins, or publishing workflows.

aiviso_is_ai_generated() is a public helper function that returns whether an attachment is declared AI-generated.

The aiviso_is_ai_generated filter adjusts the resolved attachment declaration, while aiviso_should_display_badge controls whether a qualifying Featured Image receives a badge.

Badge output can be customized through aiviso_badge_text, aiviso_badge_disclaimer, aiviso_badge_position, aiviso_badge_logo, aiviso_badge_classes, and aiviso_badge_markup. These filters apply to shared badge output, including supported Featured Image and content-image badges. Disclaimer filter values are treated as plain text.

The aiviso_multilingual_provider filter allows developers to replace the active normalized multilingual provider when implementing custom multilingual integrations.

Machine-readable disclosure integrations can use aiviso_machine_readable_metadata_enabled, aiviso_digital_source_type, aiviso_image_object, and aiviso_jsonld_graph.

Public disclosure details can be customized through aiviso_public_disclosure_detail_fields, aiviso_frontend_disclosure_details, and aiviso_disclosure_details_markup.

Post type integration is supported through aiviso_post_type_scope_types, which filters available Settings post types, and aiviso_post_type_in_scope, which allows per-post scope decisions.

Administrative integrations can use aiviso_bulk_actions to adjust supported bulk actions and aiviso_audit_capability to control access to the Audit screen.

The aiviso_disclosure_state_updated action runs after a successful central disclosure-state change, while aiviso_bulk_disclosure_updated runs after a shared bulk operation.

These APIs are intended for controlled integrations. Existing plugin settings, attachment metadata, and declaration workflows remain the primary supported behavior.

Where can I find the complete AIDisclara documentation?

The complete AIDisclara documentation includes installation instructions, configuration guides, disclosure workflows, multilingual settings, developer integrations, and troubleshooting.

Documentation is available at:

https://infinitumform.com/documentation/aidisclara
sections.changelog:
1.0.6

  • Fixed WooCommerce HPOS order editor compatibility by limiting the Featured Image status meta box to supported WordPress posts.

1.0.5

  • Added optional, language-aware tooltip disclaimers for AI-generated and AI-modified disclosure badges.
  • Added accessible click, keyboard, and delayed-hover controls with viewport-aware tooltip positioning.
  • Added safe plain-text disclaimer formatting for line breaks, bold, italic, and underline.

1.0.4

  • Renamed the public plugin name to AIDisclara.
  • Updated the complete administrative interface and documentation.
  • Updated all five translation catalogs.
  • Preserved full compatibility with the existing slug, text domain, hooks, options, and attachment metadata.

1.0.3

  • Added a Custom disclosure type for individual Media Library images.
  • Added attachment-specific custom badge text with manual WPML, Polylang, and TranslatePress language fields.
  • Added REST metadata, editor status, accessibility labels, Media Library indicators, and uninstall cleanup for custom declarations.
  • Added IPTC Digital Source Type selection, attachment disclosure details, optional publisher-supplied Schema.org JSON-LD, and safe machine-readable wrapper attributes.
  • Added Media Library disclosure filters and bulk actions, the Media > AIDisclara Audit table with CSV export, and post-type scope controls.
  • Added locally bundled official European Commission AI-content icons, with source and usage information.
  • Added an independent Badge icon-size control for built-in, custom, and EU Basic icons.
  • Added independent icon-to-text spacing and per-side badge padding controls with a live Settings preview.
  • Completed translation catalog entries for the new Badge style controls.

1.0.2

  • Added AI-modified image declarations alongside the existing AI-generated image declaration, with separately configurable badge text and shared appearance controls.

1.0.1

  • Added optional disclosure badges for AI-marked Media Library images inside individual post and public custom post type content.
  • Kept content-image disclosure limited to individual content views, excluding WordPress Pages and archive, listing, category, and search views.
  • Preserved independent Featured Image display controls, including the Everywhere scope for archive and listing contexts.
  • Improved frontend compatibility for standard Classic Editor and Gutenberg content images, including linked and captioned images.
  • Added the Serbian (Serbia) Cyrillic translation.
  • Refined the horizontal alignment of the built-in AIDisclara mark.
  • Added a cached Settings-page list of selected free plugins from the WordPress.org Plugin Directory.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
